title: Posture Slouch-Time per Work Day
dataSources: Posture readings (`posture:reading`), symptom logs (`symptom:log`), bathroom visits (`bathroom:visit`), sneeze events (`sneeze:event`).
app: Everyday body-signal logs — posture sensors, symptom and allergy journals, hydration-linked bathroom logs, and quirky personal counters — sent to Splunk HEC via wearables, MQTT, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=posture:reading
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(if(state="slouch",duration_min,0))) as slouch_min, sum(duration_min) as total by _time
| eval slouch_pct=round(100*slouch_min/total,1)
| sort - _time
description: Measures how much of each work day you spent slouching versus sitting upright, a nudge for your back.
value: Posture is hard to self-assess; a daily slouch percentage turns a vague ache into a habit you can improve.
implementation: Ingest a posture sensor into `index=personal`; review daily slouch time and percentage.
visualization: Column chart of daily slouch time as a percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It measures how much of your day you spent slouching, gently reminding you to sit up straight.
